title: finding(docs): the VS Code extension page documents five keyboard shortcuts the manifest contributes zero of
body:
`content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx` tells the reader the extension ships default keyboard shortcuts. It contributes none: `packages/vscode-extension/package.json` has no `contributes.keybindings` key at all.

Found while correcting two other false statements on the same page for objectui#7977; keyboard shortcuts are outside that card's file surface as dispatched, so this is filed separately rather than fixed there.

## The claims

The page asserts the shortcuts in five places — three inline under the command headings, plus a table introduced as `Default keyboard shortcuts:` — with line numbers on `origin/main` `59a3a233d`:

```
content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:59   **Keyboard Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+P` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd+Alt+P` (Mac)
content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:70   **Keyboard Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+V` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd+Alt+V` (Mac)
content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:108  **Keyboard Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+F` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd+Alt+F` (Mac)
content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:348  ## Keyboard Shortcuts
content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:357  | Export to React | `Ctrl+Alt+E` | `Cmd+Alt+E` |
```

The table adds a fourth binding, `Ctrl+Alt+E` for Export to React, which has no inline claim of its own; the Development Workflow section then hands all of them to the reader as instructions (`content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:407` — `**Export** - Convert to React (Ctrl+Alt+E)`).

## The measurement

`contributes.keybindings` in `packages/vscode-extension/package.json` reads `null` — the key is absent. A grep over the package for any keybinding contribution or any of the documented chords returns nothing:

```
grep -rn "keybinding|Ctrl+Alt|ctrl+alt" packages/vscode-extension --include=*.json --include=*.ts --include=*.md -i   (node_modules excluded)
   0 hits
```

Live control on the same corpus and the same tool, so the zero is a reading and not a broken search:

```
packages/vscode-extension/src/extension.ts:97   vscode.commands.registerCommand('objectui.exportToReact', async () => {
packages/vscode-extension/package.json:91         "command": "objectui.exportToReact",
packages/vscode-extension/package.json:124        "command": "objectui.exportToReact",
```

The six commands are contributed and reachable from the Command Palette and the context menus, which the page also documents correctly. Only the key chords are fictional: a reader who presses `Ctrl+Alt+P` gets whatever their own keymap has bound there, which on stock VS Code is nothing.

## A second, weaker mismatch on the same page

`ObjectUI: Create New Schema` is documented (`:116`) as `Select template (Dashboard, Form, Grid, etc.)`. The templates `createNewSchema()` actually offers (`packages/vscode-extension/src/extension.ts:249-255`) are `Empty Schema`, `Simple Form`, `Dashboard`, `Card Layout`, `Data Table`. `Grid` is not one of them, and only `Dashboard` carries the documented label verbatim. The `etc.` hedges it, so this is softer than the shortcuts, but it is the same page and the same class and a fix would land in the same stroke.

## Which way to fix is a maintainer's call

Two directions, and they are not equivalent:

1. **Correct the page** — delete the shortcut table and the three inline claims, keep the Command Palette and context-menu routes that are true, and point the reader at VS Code's own Keyboard Shortcuts editor to bind the commands themselves. The page already documents that editor at `:361`.
2. **Make the page true** — add a `contributes.keybindings` block to the manifest with the documented chords. That is a product change, not a docs change, and the chords want their own judgement before they ship.

## Why nothing catches it

Same blind spot the triage on objectui#7977 recorded, one surface over: the doc gates that read `content/docs` check fence languages, snippet types, component `type` literals and links. None of them compares a documented claim about the extension against that extension's manifest. Related to the same cluster objectui#7976 / objectui#7974 / objectui#7837 name, all of which are about a document mirroring something no tool re-derives.

Filed unassigned by the os-dev seat working objectui#7977 on branch `claude/issue-7977-vscode-export-page-prose`. Generated by Claude Code, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr` (attribution written as prose because issue-creation strips the footer block).
